D is the correct answer! Source of service income is where the service is performed. Source of business income is where goods are sold or business transaction takes place. Source of rental income for fixed property is where property is located. Where income is derived from more than one source it may need to be apportioned between those sources. Source of a capital gain is determined by the nature of the CGT asset and the activities of the taxpayer. Source of a loss is where the loss is incurred. Source of a net capital loss is where the net capital loss for the year is worked out. Source of an annuity is where the annuity is purchased or where the lump sum amount from which the annuity is derived would have been assessed on a property basis. Source of a royalty is where the royalty is paid. Source of an interest income is where the money is paid or due for payment. Source of a dividend income is where the company is located. Source of a partnership income is where the partnership is located. Source of an Australian resident's income is where the economic activity of the taxpayer is located. Source of a foreign resident's income is where the income is derived.

A is the correct answer. According to s 6(1) (b), an individual is a tax resident of Australia under the domicile test where his or her domicile is in Australia. The Commissioner is satisfied that the domicile of a person is in Australia where the person considers that he or she has his or her permanent place of abode in Australia and the person is physically present in Australia for more than six months of the income year. However, the domicile test does not apply where the individual can demonstrate that he or she does not have a “permanent place of abode outside Australia” (s 6(1) (c)).

The correct answer is E!A statutory income is income specified in tax legislation, as opposed to other kinds of income which are not referred to in tax legislation.Statutory income can be categorised into two broad groups:1. First class statutory income: this is income that is stated to be assessable by a specific provision in the ITAA36 or ITAA97, eg, capital gains.2. Second class statutory income: this is income that is not automatically assessable under the ITAA36 or ITAA97 but is required to be included in assessable income by a specific provision in the legislation, eg, dividends, rent from a lease and royalties.
